addendum: Wikipedia-led tests, addendum l: books chosen by what was known at each month, the calendar month in the library model, fewer duplicate Wikipedia features, and the ridge penalty chosen inside the training data
status: Fixed 2026-10-30 01:04 +07 after Khant reviewed the draft written at 00:55 and answered "Fix it and start" (about 01:03). The text below is the draft unchanged except this field and fixed_on. Nothing of this addendum had run when it was fixed.
parent_record: prereg/wiki_led_settings_2026-10-20.json, addenda a to k; their settings apply unless changed here
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai, who chose on 30 Oct 2026 (about 00:45 +07) 'Books-in-time + month': books chosen by what was known at each month and the calendar month in the library model, with the feature clean-up and the ridge penalty
why: A check of the thesis against the AIC-400 data wrangling checklist (paper/Course_Standards_Crosscheck_2026-10-30_0026.md) found two things worth changing in the method. (1) Test A's books were chosen by at least 500 loans in 2016 to 2026 and by having an English article in 2026, a look-ahead in the choice of books that the methods list as their main limit; missing Wikipedia features before an article existed still mark a book that will later gain one. (2) The library-only model's errors follow the calendar month (2019 to 2023 only, see seen_before_fixing). It also found near-duplicate Wikipedia features and a ridge penalty fixed at 1 without any choice inside the training data.

L1_books_chosen_in_time.rows: Test D's corrected definitions (code/main_study/wiki_led/60c_test_d_rows.py: one series per work and format, eligible at origin t when its loans over t-11..t sum to at least 24; Test A's L, M6, D, Sg, Y, history features and excluded months), restricted to the fixed 25% sample of all Seattle works (md5 of work_id, first hex digit 0 to 3): 43,303 works, 1,773,978 rows, 1,259,084 of them at scored origins (2019-01 to 2026-07). The 5,804 Test A works outside the sample are not added, because they were chosen by later loans. Works in data/db/taxonomy_v3/quality/placeholder_works.csv (bundles of items, DEVIATIONS 30 Oct 00:36) are left out.
L1_books_chosen_in_time.book_articles: Every sampled work, whatever its loans, is matched with the rules and the stored bulk Wikidata table of code/study2r/02_match_books.py: the ISBN-13 of the work's Seattle records against the ISBNs of written-work items and their editions; else the Seattle title equal to the Wikidata label or Wikipedia title (parenthesis and leading article removed) and a creator's family name a word of an item author. The bulk table is the stored one of 14 October 2026 (88,540 items with an English article), not refreshed. The 1,943 sampled works matched in Test A keep their match.
L1_books_chosen_in_time.author_articles: The author article of the matched book item (Test A's route, data/db/study2r/book_author_articles.parquet); for every other work, the first author parsed from the creator and matched by Test B's rules (code/main_study/wiki_led/02_author_match.py: the name, then '(writer)', '(author)', '(novelist)'; accepted when the Wikidata item is a human), reusing Test B's cache (19,796 of the 24,493 sampled creators already tried, 8,898 of them matched; 4,697 to try, at most 5 requests a second). Works with an empty creator have no author article.
L1_books_chosen_in_time.views: Daily user views of every new article, 2015-07-01 to 2026-09-30, from the Wikimedia per-article service at most 3 requests a second, cached: book articles with redirects screened as in code/study2r/03_pageviews.py, author articles by canonical title. Weekly shares of all English Wikipedia user views as in code/study2r/04_weekly_series.py.
L1_books_chosen_in_time.point_in_time: A Wikipedia feature at origin t uses only weeks that ended by the last day of t and is missing before the article's first week with views (addendum e's correction). A work with no article, or whose article has no views yet, has missing features, so a missing value no longer marks a book that will later gain an article. The links come from the stored Wikidata table, so which works have a link is still taken from later knowledge (a smaller look-ahead than Test A's, in the links only, not in views or loans); reported as a limit.

L2_calendar_month: Two calendar features are added to the library-history model: the calendar month of the target month (1 to 12, a categorical feature in LightGBM) and its number of days. They enter the library models only; Wikipedia-only models stay Wikipedia-only (principle 1).
L3_feature_cleanup: Wikipedia features per article: Test A's nine minus nrise8 and rmax, so 7 per article and 14 for the book and author articles. nrise8 nearly repeats dw (Spearman 0.997 on Test A rows of test years 2019 to 2023) and rmax nearly repeats r4 (0.90 for books, 0.92 for authors) and is computed differently in the code and in the record (audit A3). The 18-feature set is run beside as a check.
L4_ridge_penalty: W_ridge: for each test year, alpha is chosen from {0.1, 1, 10, 100} by mean absolute error on the last 12 training origins (time split), the model for each alpha fitted on the training rows whose target month is on or before the first of those origins, as the benchmark does (code/main_study/study4/_models.py, choose_alpha; the grid and rule of prereg/forecast_settings_2026-10-13.json); then refitted on all training rows with that alpha. Features standardized on training rows only; a missing value becomes 0 with a 0/1 missing indicator.

models.walk_forward: Test years 2019 to 2026; a model for test year Y is fitted only on rows whose target month ended before 1 January of Y. LightGBM settings of Tests A and D (300 trees, learning rate 0.05, 31 leaves, at least 50 rows per leaf, 80% of rows and columns per tree, seed 20261020), all formats pooled with format as a feature, one model for the change D and one for the level Y. Nothing is tuned except the ridge penalty of L4.

list.naive: Repeat last month for the level; the naive change ln(1+L(t)) - ln(1+M6) as the ranking.
list.H: Library history features of Test D plus format.
list.HM: H plus the two calendar features of L2.
list.W14: LightGBM on the 14 Wikipedia features of L3.
list.W14_ridge: Ridge on the 14 features with the penalty of L4.
list.W18: LightGBM on Test A's 18 features (check of L3, and the bridge to Test D).
list.HW18: H plus the 18 features: Test D's HW on the new rows (bridge to Test D).

measures: Test D's: change rank (Spearman between predicted and actual D within each format and origin month, averaged over format-months); share of each month's top 20 and top 50 that rose (D at least ln 1.5), lists drawn within each format and pooled; the same among rows not yet risen (ln(1+L(t)) - ln(1+M6) below ln 1.5); surge average precision over the surge rate; level: mean absolute error of Y, and in loans (expm1 of the prediction, floored at 0) the mean and median absolute error and the share within 2 loans. Each for all formats and by format, over 2019 to 2026 and 2024 to 2026. Because most sampled works have no article, the Wikipedia-only models are also scored on rows with at least one article feature (descriptive). Intervals: 2,000 draws of blocks of 3 consecutive scored months, seed 20261020, differences paired by month.

decisions.L1: Wikipedia alone, books chosen in time: W14 change rank has a 95% interval above 0.
decisions.L2a: Wikipedia adds to the library, books chosen in time: HMW14 minus HM change rank, paired by month, has an interval above 0.
decisions.L2b: The same for the early-warning list: HMW14 minus HM share of the top 20 that rose, among rows not yet risen, has an interval above 0.
decisions.L3: The calendar month helps: HM minus H mean absolute error of Y, paired by month, has an interval below 0. (A shift shared by every book in a month cannot change within-month ranks, so this is judged on the level; its effect on ranks is reported beside.)
decisions.descriptive: W18 and HW18 against W14 and HMW14 (cost of the clean-up); W18 and HW18 on these rows against Test D's stored W and HW (how much the choice of books moved the numbers); everything else.

blind_test.forecasts: After the backtest, H, HM, W14 and HMW14 are fitted on every row of the frame whose target month is 2026-08 or earlier and rank every eligible sampled work at origin 2026-08 (target 2026-09). The forecasts (CSV) are frozen, their SHA-256 written into prereg/README.md, and both made public on GitHub before any month after 2026-08 is downloaded or read. On 30 Oct 2026, 00:48 +07, the library's API held months up to 2026-08 only (28_final_test_download.py --list).
blind_test.scoring: When 2026-09 is downloaded under the final test's rules (code/main_study/benchmark/28_final_test_download.py, calendar order; new records matched to works by key as in 29_final_test_world.py), each sampled work's September loans per format are counted and scored once: change rank within each format over all eligible works, and the top-20 share that rose (lists within format, 60 slots), with intervals from 2,000 bootstrap draws of works (seed 20261030) and exact binomial intervals for the lists.
blind_test.decision_LB: HMW14 minus HM change rank in September 2026, paired over works, has an interval above 0. One month is a small test and is reported as such.
blind_test.fallback: If 2026-09 is downloaded before these forecasts are frozen, the blind test moves to origin 2026-09 (target 2026-10), frozen before 2026-10 is downloaded; if that also cannot be done, there is no blind test and the backtest is reported as not blind. This addendum never delays or changes the final test or the live October lists.

order_of_work: 1 matching and downloads (no loans read except the eligibility already stored); 2 rows and features, with a data report; 3 backtest and report; 4 frozen forecasts at origin 2026-08 and their publication; 5 scoring once when 2026-09 is downloaded. Nothing is rerun after a result except to fix a logged coding error.
seen_before_fixing: All results of Tests A to F and addenda h to k, including Test D's scores on its rows (the 25% sample plus the Test A works); Test D's scores on the sampled works alone were never computed. Read-only checks of 30 Oct 2026: the placeholder bundles and Test D without them; on Test A's stored corrected predictions for test years 2019 to 2023 only, the library-only model's mean residual by target calendar month (-0.056 in February to +0.064 in January, +0.050 in July and August, -0.043 in November) and the Spearman correlations of the Wikipedia features. Sizing counts of this record (works, rows, matches already stored, creators already tried). The API's month list (up to 2026-08). No feature, model or score of this addendum exists.
known_limits: The 2019 to 2026 backtest is not blind: Test D's results on overlapping rows and the residual pattern by month on 2019 to 2023 were seen. Only the September 2026 test is blind.
Links come from today's Wikidata, so whether a work has a link at all still uses later knowledge.
Most sampled works will have no article; the Wikipedia-only models then rank most rows by 'no article', and their result describes the whole library, not books with pages.
The calendar month is shared by every book in a month, so it can change within-month ranks only through its interactions with other features in the trees.
One library; loans are capped by copies and licences and do not record holds.
